newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lagerfeld brings sheer elegance to Chanel.
newsitem.headline: Lagerfeld brings sheer elegance to Chanel.

text.p: German designer Karl Lagerfeld's styling for the emaciated reached new heights on Tuesday in a couture collection for Chanel that personified pure refinement.

Lagerfeld, who has succeeded during his 14 years at Chanel in remaining faithful to the in-house spirit while introducing modern touches, unveiled skinny glove-fitting black tweed jackets, void of decoration but for pearl buttons or the clasp of a diamond brooch.

Over wide trousers of featherweight fluid wool or narrow, translucent skirts of black chiffon with wave-edged hemlines at mid-calf, they formed dark, sinewy silhouettes against the cream-coloured walls of the Ritz hotel suite venue.

It was pure class with an edgy restraint, from the white cuffs of a pert organza blouse to the bracelet sleeves of a neat trademark tweed and the wide-brimmed straw hats curtained with black widow mesh.
But the show begged the question of what happens to those nervous, slim silhouettes when the fashions are donned by Chanel's matronly customers.
Dream on, Lagerfeld seemed to be saying when he sent out the models wearing Chanel's $30,000 diamond earrings.
A flash of colour appeared in a sleek raspberry coat, a sugar pink satin jumpsuit or the floral bridal dress, Lagerfeld's one and only concession to prints.

Evening came with a 1920s flavour in tube beading on smoky, diaphanous chiffon, a series of slim terracotta tulle gowns with jet embroidery and the feathers perched on slim wire ornaments wobbling on the supermodels' hair.
"It was absolutely amazing. The height of refinement. The scalloping, the edging, the make-up -- everything was perfect," said Joseph Boitano of U.S. department stores Bergdorf Goodman.
"That's how a couture customer wants to look," he added.

Aside from voluptuous Naomi Campbell and swanlike Shalom Harlow, the supermodels have been scarce this season. A handful have made their only appearances at Chanel and in John Galliano's collection for Christian Dior on Monday.

Kiki Feraud, daughter of retired French designer Louis Feraud, took off in the opposite direction from Lagerfeld, fastening gold hardware bibs on African motif crepes, rows of brass buttons on a blue bellbottomed jumpsuit and table napkins on a creamy skirt.
Like the military jackets with gold braid, Feraud's fortuny-pleated silver gown with bumpy seams and over-sized Aladdin turbans of crumpled gauze, the collection cried out for a lighter touch.
